title: FP8/INT8 Optimize recommendations — UI copy draft + eligibility constraints (WIP)
content:
Context
- Optimize will start surfacing recommendations around quantized kernel modes (FP8 + INT8) as part of the FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint.
- Goal: help customers capture cost/latency wins without accidentally opting into quality or reliability regressions.
- This doc is UI copy + constraints only (not final policy, not final numbers).

Audience / surfaces
1) Optimize Console → “Recommendations” feed (card UI)
2) Optimize Console → Model settings page (per model / per deployment mode)
3) API/SDK (optional later): response headers or console banner (NOT in scope for v1)

Non-goals (for v1)
- We are NOT promising specific % improvements in-product (per Irene/Henry transparency thread). We can show measured deltas for the customer’s own traffic if/when we have enough samples.
- We are NOT providing a universal “FP8 is always faster” message.
- We are NOT enabling quantization by default through Optimize. Recommendation should guide user to a safe config change, with gating.

Terminology (UI-safe)
- “Kernel mode” (preferred) vs “quantization mode” (more ML-y). Proposed: user-facing = “Kernel mode” with tooltip: “Uses lower-precision kernels (FP8/INT8) where supported.”
- FP8: “FP8 (beta)” label initially.
- INT8: “INT8 (beta)” label initially.
- Baseline: “Standard” (no quantized kernels).

Eligibility constraints (when we can show the recommendation)
Hard requirements (must be true)
- Model is in hosted catalog AND has a supported FP8 or INT8 variant in model registry (server-side truth).
- Runtime dispatch supports the mode for the current GPU architecture in the customer’s region (ex: H100 yes, A100 maybe, L4 limited) — do not show a recommendation that can’t be enabled.
- Perf canary status: green for this {model, kernel mode, GPU SKU, region} with current runtime release (or within allowed skew). Canary failure or active rollback => suppress recommendations and show an informational banner only.
- Applied ML / Evals sign-off: for defaults we need sign-off; for recommendations we still need a “safe to suggest” flag per model family (from Arjun/Jonas policy). If sign-off is missing, recommendation can be shown only as “experimental / requires eval,” but product preference is to suppress entirely for v1.

Soft requirements (should be true)
- We have benchmark evidence for at least one representative workload regime matching the customer’s traffic cluster: prompt length bucket + output length bucket + concurrency. If unknown, show with weaker wording and stronger disclaimer.
- No known open incidents / support escalations tied to this mode in the customer’s region in last N days.

Explicit suppressions (do NOT recommend)
- Customers in regulated mode / stricter SLO contracts where any output drift is unacceptable unless they explicitly enable “allow quantization experiments” in console.
- Models flagged by Applied ML for known long-context quality regression under FP8 (see eng-ml thread) until mitigated.
- Regions/clusters with driver/CUDA mismatch or known instability.

User knobs we expect exist (or need to add)
- Per model setting: Kernel mode = Standard / FP8 (beta) / INT8 (beta)
- Optional: “Fallback on error/regression” toggle (enabled by default), with a short explanation.
- Visibility: Show “Supported on: H100 (us-east, us-west), A100 (us-east)” etc.

Recommendation types (v1)
A) “Switch to FP8” (latency/throughput oriented)
B) “Switch to INT8” (cost oriented / throughput where FP8 is not supported)
C) “Stay on Standard” (explicitly tell user not to switch if risk is high; this reduces pressure to ‘recommend something’)

Recommendation card — proposed structure
Title (short)
- FP8: “Try FP8 kernels for faster generation”
- INT8: “Try INT8 kernels to reduce cost per token”

Subtitle (1 line)
- FP8: “Recommended for this model on H100 when prompt+decode mix matches your traffic.”
- INT8: “Recommended for this model when quality checks pass and INT8 kernels are supported in your region.”

Body copy (2–3 lines, conservative)
Variant 1 (FP8)
- “FP8 can improve tokens/sec and lower p95 latency for common shapes. Enable behind a safety fallback and monitor TTFT/TPOT.”
Variant 2 (INT8)
- “INT8 can reduce compute cost for supported shapes. Output quality may change slightly; run an eval on your prompt set before enabling broadly.”

Impact preview (ONLY if we have customer-specific evidence)
- Header: “Estimated impact (last 24h sample)”
- Lines:
  - “p95 latency: -X% (±Y%)”
  - “tokens/sec: +X% (±Y%)”
  - “error rate: no change”
- If sample is too small: “Not enough traffic to estimate impact yet.” (do not show numbers)

CTA
- Primary: “Review & enable”
- Secondary: “Learn more”
- Tertiary (small): “Run quick quality check” (links to eval harness instructions / internal now; external later)

Footer disclaimers (always present, short)
- “Beta: Performance and quality can vary by prompt length, batch size, and region.”
- “You can roll back instantly. We’ll automatically fall back to Standard if error rates spike.” (only if this is true; confirm with Rafael)

Tooltip / “Learn more” popover copy
Tooltip label: “What are FP8/INT8 kernels?”
Body:
- “These modes use lower-precision GPU kernels for parts of inference. This can improve throughput and reduce cost on supported GPUs.”
- “Trade-offs: Some workloads see no benefit, and quality can vary by model and prompt characteristics.”
- Link: “Benchmark methodology” (points to public-safe doc later; internal now)

Model settings page copy
Section label: “Kernel mode”
Helper text:
- “Choose how this model runs on supported GPUs. Quantized modes (FP8/INT8) can improve performance but may affect output quality.”
Options (radio)
- Standard (recommended default)
  - Description: “Full-precision kernels. Most consistent across workloads.”
- FP8 (beta)
  - Description: “Faster on supported GPUs for common shapes. May affect output quality on some long-context prompts.”
- INT8 (beta)
  - Description: “Lower compute cost on supported shapes. Requires calibration; may affect output quality.”

Safety controls (checkboxes)
- [x] “Auto-fallback to Standard on elevated errors or latency regressions”
  - Helper: “Fallback triggers are based on TTFT/TPOT and error-rate thresholds from perf canary.”
- [ ] “Enable only for canary traffic (10%)”
  - Helper: “We’ll gradually ramp and pause if metrics regress.”

Confirmation modal copy (when enabling FP8/INT8)
Title:
- “Enable FP8 (beta)?” / “Enable INT8 (beta)?”
Body (FP8):
- “FP8 can improve throughput and latency on supported GPUs. Performance may vary by prompt distribution and concurrency.”
- “Before ramping above 10%, validate:
  - TTFT and TPOT on your key routes
  - Quality on a representative prompt set
  - Error rate remains stable”
Body (INT8):
- “INT8 can reduce compute cost for supported shapes. Output quality may change slightly. We recommend running an eval on your prompt set.”
Buttons:
- Primary: “Enable for 10% canary”
- Secondary: “Enable for 100% (not recommended)” (consider removing; product leaning: don’t offer for v1)
- Cancel: “Cancel”

Empty / ineligible states
1) Not supported GPU/region
- Banner: “FP8/INT8 kernels aren’t available in your current region or GPU tier.”
- Action: “View supported regions”

2) Temporarily disabled due to canary/rollback
- Banner: “Quantized kernels are temporarily disabled due to a detected regression.”
- Subtext: “We’re investigating and will re-enable after canary is green.”

3) Quality sign-off missing
- Banner: “FP8/INT8 recommendation not available for this model yet.”
- Subtext: “This model requires additional quality validation before we can recommend quantized kernels.”

Do’s / Don’ts (performance transparency constraints)
Do
- Use “can,” “may,” “observed in benchmarks,” “for supported GPUs/shapes.”
- Prefer “based on your traffic sample” for any shown deltas.
- Always mention variability and the need to monitor TTFT/TPOT.

Don’t
- Don’t claim universal improvements (“FP8 is faster”, “INT8 is cheaper”) without qualifiers.
- Don’t present sprint benchmark numbers as customer-specific outcomes.
- Don’t imply quality parity unless Jonas/Arjun explicitly sign off for that model family + workload regime.

Content placeholders we still need (TODO)
- Final naming: “Kernel mode” vs “Precision mode” vs “Quantized kernels”.
- Exact gating source-of-truth fields (where we read these flags): model registry vs runtime capability service.
- Confirm fallback behavior language with Rafael (SRE). Do we truly auto-fallback on latency, or only on errors? (Copy must match reality.)
- Define “enough traffic” threshold to show impact preview (Allison: sample size guidance).
- Whether we expose “beta” label in UI or keep it in tooltip only.

Proposed internal policy mapping → UI rendering (rough)
- If {canary=green AND eval=green AND runtime_supported=true}:
  - show recommendation card + allow enable
- If {runtime_supported=true AND (canary!=green OR eval!=green)}:
  - no recommendation; show info banner “not available” + link
- If {runtime_supported=false}:
  - no mention (avoid confusing customers) OR show disabled option on settings page only

Review notes from stakeholders (captured inline)
- Henry: copy should avoid any % claims unless tied to customer traffic sample, and even then show error bars.
- Jonas: any suggestion must have at least a lightweight quality sanity pass for that model family; long-context caveat should be explicit for FP8 where applicable.
- Allison: TTFT/TPOT terms need tooltips; many customers don’t know them.

Draft tooltips for TTFT/TPOT (if we show metrics)
- TTFT: “Time to first token. Measures how quickly streaming starts.”
- TPOT: “Time per output token. Measures generation speed after the first token.”

Appendix: internal references (for product reviewers)
- Methodology: sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/kernel-benchmarking-methodology-top-hosted-models.json
- Heuristics ADR: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-019-fp8-int8-kernel-selection-heuristics.json
- Quant profile policy: sources/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/fp8-int8-profile-policy-for-hosted-catalog.json
- Perf standards: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/performance-standards/benchmarking-standards-fp8-int8.json
- Canary runbook: sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/perf-canary-rollout-for-new-kernels.json

Open questions
- Should Optimize recommend FP8 vs INT8 separately, or decide internally and present a single “Recommended mode”?
- Can we safely say “automatic fallback” for latency regressions, or only for error spikes? (Need confirmation from perf-canary implementation ENG-7426.)
- Should we add a “Run eval” CTA that triggers our eval harness, or just link out? (Probably link out for v1.)

Change log
- 2026-02-14: initial draft (Aditya)
- 2026-02-18: added transparency constraints + removed hard % claims (per Irene/Henry thread)
- 2026-02-21: added explicit suppressions + eligibility (per Jonas/Arjun feedback)
- 2026-02-26: updated confirmation modal + empty states; added TTFT/TPOT tooltips (per Allison)
